brief.topic: Two Circles Sharing a Mechanical Rhythm

s01: Two gears can turn together without turning at the same speed.
The smaller one completes its circles more often.
Come closer to their shared teeth.
These gears have the same tooth spacing.
One has sixteen teeth, and the other has thirty two.
A full turn of the small gear passes sixteen teeth through the meeting region.
That advances the large gear by only half a turn.
Another sixteen teeth complete the large circle.
The two gears turn in opposite directions.
Their angular speeds follow the inverse ratio of their tooth counts.
Twice as many teeth means half as many turns in the same time.
The drawn teeth are schematic; the ratio assumes proper engagement.
Now let the larger gear drive the smaller one.
One large turn produces two small turns.
The relationship survives this exchange of roles.
A quiet mechanical rhythm comes from counting what passes between two circles.

scenes.narration:
Two gears can turn together without turning at the same speed. The smaller one completes its circles more often.

Come closer to their shared teeth. These gears have the same tooth spacing. One has sixteen teeth, and the other has thirty two.

A full turn of the small gear passes sixteen teeth through the meeting region. That advances the large gear by only half a turn. Another sixteen teeth complete the large circle. The two gears turn in opposite directions.

Their angular speeds follow the inverse ratio of their tooth counts. Twice as many teeth means half as many turns in the same time. The drawn teeth are schematic; the ratio assumes proper engagement.

Now let the larger gear drive the smaller one. One large turn produces two small turns. The relationship survives this exchange of roles. A quiet mechanical rhythm comes from counting what passes between two circles.
